g.ei's: forma che non esiste: ei è irregolare (eieren)

hard.q: De ___ in Vlaanderen zijn mooi: Gent, Brugge, Leuven...
hard.e: Plurale irregolare: stad → steden (cambia anche la vocale). Non stadden.

hard.e: Irregolare: schip → schepen, con la vocale che cambia da i a e. Non schippen.
hard.tt: Vedo tre navi nel porto di Anversa.

en.note:
The idea

Like English, Dutch makes plurals by adding an ending. But instead of one main ending (-s) there are two: -en and -s. And in the plural the article is always de, just as English always uses "the".

Which ending?

  • -en is the general rule: boek → boeken, fiets → fietsen.
  • -s for words ending in -el, -em, -en, -er, -je (weak final syllable): tafel → tafels, meisje → meisjes, kamer → kamers.
  • -'s (with an apostrophe) for words ending in a, i, o, u, y: auto → auto's, menu → menu's. The apostrophe keeps the vowel long.

Spelling with -en

Same logic as the verbs (unit 2): the sound stays the same, the spelling changes.

  • A long vowel written double becomes single, because the syllable opens up: boom → bo-men, jaar → ja-ren.
  • Short vowel: double the consonant to keep it short: man → man-nen, bus → bus-sen.
  • f → v and s → z between two vowels: brief → brieven, huis → huizen.

Irregulars to memorize

singularplural
het kindde kinderen
het eide eieren
de stadde steden
het schipde schepen

Watch out: typical mistakes for English speakers

  • Adding -s everywhere, English-style: boeks → boeken.
  • Keeping the double vowel: boomen → bomen.
  • Forgetting the apostrophe: autos → auto's.
  • Using het in the plural: het kinderen → de kinderen.
en.vlaams: In Belgium French fries are frieten (de friet, de frieten) and you buy them at a frituur or "frietkot". In the Netherlands you'd say "patat". In everyday speech, especially in the Netherlands, the final -n of the plural is often dropped: "boeke".

items.e: Long vowel in an open syllable: bomen.

g.boekken: not a real form: oe stays as it is

g.tafel's: the apostrophe is only used after a vowel

g.manen: moons: with one n the a becomes long

drills.e: Open syllable: the long vowel is written single, bomen.

g.boomen: not a real form: oo becomes o

drills.e: s becomes z between two vowels: huizen.

g.huisen: not a real form: s → z

hard.q: Ik koop op de markt in Antwerpen drie ___ en twee kilo kaas.
hard.e: ei is irregular: eieren (like kinderen). Note twee kilo, though: after a number, units of measure stay singular.

g.eien: not a real form: ei is irregular
g.ei's: not a real form: ei is irregular (eieren)

hard.tt: I buy three eggs and two kilos of cheese at the market in Antwerp.

o: De menu's in het frietkot zijn nieuw.
Het menu's in het frietkot zijn nieuw.
De menus in het frietkot zijn nieuw.
De menu's in het frietkot is nieuw.
hard.e: In the plural the article is always de (even though it's het menu), after -u you need -'s, and the verb is plural: zijn.

The menus at the frietkot are new.
wrong: plural subject, so the verb is zijn

hard.tt: The menus at the frietkot are new.

hard.q: De ___ in Vlaanderen zijn mooi: Gent, Brugge, Leuven...
hard.e: Irregular plural: stad → steden (the vowel changes too). Not stadden.
hard.tt: The cities in Flanders are beautiful: Ghent, Bruges, Leuven...

hard.q: Ik zie drie ___ in de haven van Antwerpen.
hard.e: Irregular: schip → schepen, with the vowel changing from i to e. Not schippen.
hard.tt: I see three ships in the port of Antwerp.

hard.q: The girls have three bikes and two cars.
a: De meisjes hebben drie fietsen en twee auto's

hard.q: The men buy fries at the frietkot.
a: De mannen kopen frieten in het frietkot
De mannen kopen frieten bij het frietkot
De mannen kopen friet in het frietkot
De mannen kopen friet bij het frietkot
De mannen kopen frieten aan het frietkot
De mannen kopen friet aan het frietkot
hard.e: mannen: short vowel, so the n doubles. In Belgium fries are frieten (or friet), not patat.

hard.q: The men are looking for the car keys.
hard.a: De mannen zoeken de sleutels van de auto
hard.e: sleutel ends in -el: plural sleutels. In the plural the article is always de. Note that Dutch says de sleutels van de auto ("the keys of the car").
hard.tt: The men are looking for the car keys.

hard.q: The girls are giving us three books tomorrow.
hard.a: De meisjes geven ons morgen drie boeken
alt: Morgen geven de meisjes ons drie boeken
hard.e: meisjes and boeken; the object pronoun is ons (not wij), and the verb is plural: geven. Dutch uses the simple present for this (geven, not "are giving").
hard.tt: The girls are giving us three books tomorrow.
